reads.best: Ambitious native audio capture and overlay pipeline with very large tests, docs, screenshots and failure messages; key kept in secret store.

reads.best: Finished like a product, with driverless Core Audio capture, themed screenshots, a minimal child environment and heavy fakes-based tests.
reads.worst: macOS only (Windows a preview, Linux planned) and it needs an ElevenLabs key; the README still has a pending live capture.

reads.best: It adds a novel middleware-level progress signal across different commands, and tests exercise both warnings and actual pre-execution blocking.
reads.worst: It only fingerprints bounded local workspace samples, so remote effects and changes outside the selected workspace cannot count as progress; enforce mode is not an authorization boundary.

reads.best: It combines a real Desktop UI, guarded secret-store access, quota caching, and a durable local usage ledger into a product-quality operational view.
reads.worst: Several provider cards are necessarily limited by unavailable provider or Hermes usage APIs, and the full UI is not covered by end-to-end tests.

reads.best: It combines a real model provider, authenticated local proxy, live offer routing and a Desktop seller switcher with extensive tests.
reads.worst: The pinned release lacks a paid end-to-end reply and installed Desktop seller-switch test, and operation needs a funded marketplace key.

reads.best: It turns practical data-loss prevention and statistical disclosure controls into a large, policy-driven, tested agent egress boundary.
reads.worst: Its parsers are deliberately heuristic and cannot certify safe disclosure or catch every network-exfiltration form.

reads.best: Brings research-data-centre output vetting to agents in code outside the model, including secondary suppression so a hidden cell cannot be recovered from totals, with a broad test suite.
reads.worst: Upload detection is pattern matching that a determined command can slip past, and fail_mode defaults to open on internal errors.

reads.best: The payment gate combines owner-issued limits, transaction simulation, one-use approvals, tests, and a Desktop audit view.
reads.worst: Setup persists the private key in Hermes’ .env, and standing grants permit unattended payments.

reads.best: Deterministic pre-sign checks, revocable budgets and approval escalation give agent payments meaningful controls beyond a wallet tool.
reads.worst: Its scope is Solana transfers and its safety model still trusts the configured RPC and the Hermes process holding the signing key.

reads.best: Fixes a real Hermes gap (cua-driver failing on Wayland/Hyprland) by swapping the computer_use backend, backed by an extensively tested CLI.
reads.worst: Niche audience (Hyprland users only) and requires a separate hypruse install.

reads.best: Idempotent card links, secrets via profile secret scope, broad tests, screenshots.
reads.worst: Needs Linear/Jira setup, so it fits teams already on those trackers.

reads.best: Hash-bound approvals, fail-closed namespace policy and a durable replay journal turn workflow repair into a controlled Hermes capability.
reads.worst: Setup is involved and depends on a private approval-bypass API; Kestra lacks atomic flow updates, leaving a documented concurrent-edit window.

reads.best: Version checks, idempotent writes, shared agent/UI storage and extensive workflow tests turn CRM records into a substantial native Hermes workspace.
reads.worst: It is explicitly a small-workspace prototype with bounded legacy lists, incomplete platform/accessibility coverage and no email or external CRM connectors.

reads.best: Combines real approval hooks, correction-driven grant revocation and tool-log handoffs with a documented dashboard and extensive focused tests.
reads.worst: The extra pre-tool gate catches internal exceptions and returns no directive, so its added protection can fail open; earned trust also rests on heuristic action classification.

reads.best: It turns many parallel agent chats into one answerable queue: classification goes through Hermes's own model API, answers go into the chat composer after a five-second undo window, and it has screenshots, a changelog and a written list of known gaps.
reads.worst: The shipped desktop/plugin.js is a minified 260 KB bundle (source is in src/), it reads other profiles' state.db files straight from disk and leans on private Hermes internals, and its 36 JS and about 49 Python test files are run by no CI.

reads.best: Fails closed on any registry outage or unknown result, holds no keys and sends no transactions itself, and routes payment gating through Hermes's native approval prompt rather than auto-approving.
reads.worst: EVM-testnet-only in this release, and its payment-shaped-call detection relies on regex heuristics on tool names/args that the README itself admits can miss some payment shapes (e.g. wallet-server-settled payments).

reads.best: Middleware exposes provider-level signals a skill cannot access, with heat maps and native human approval rather than automatic execution.
reads.worst: Requires non-streaming compatible providers, adds a model request per guarded call, and lets calls through when scoring fails or re-derivations disagree too much.

reads.best: It catches whole-table writes (WHERE 1=1, no WHERE) that Hermes's shape-based detector lets run, with a concrete comparison table.
reads.worst: Only helps users whose agent runs SQL through the shell; it needs to parse each client's commands.

reads.best: Opens the iPhone's Shortcuts surface to Hermes from Linux with no Mac, verifying compiled output, decoding LZFSE/AEA in pure Python and refusing builds without a sandbox.
reads.worst: Linux-only, needs an external Cherri compiler, and signing uploads the shortcut to a third-party service (RoutineHub), so it rests on tools it does not control.

reads.best: A substantive geospatial engine computes pixel-based measurements with provenance, cloud handling and tests, then presents them through polished Hermes media surfaces.
reads.worst: Spectral thresholds can confuse seasonal change or land clearing with damage, and the image cache grows without automatic pruning.

reads.best: A small dependency-free lifecycle guard catches repeated failed code reached through different edit calls.
reads.worst: It only tracks write_file and patch, attributes a failed check to every dirty file, and lets the same failed version through on retry.

reads.best: A complete maintenance workflow combines approval-gated changes, unattended-run guards, credential-safe redirects and extensive privacy and connector tests.
reads.worst: Updates have no backup or rollback, and the optional direct 1Password CLI credential route is less aligned with catalog secret-scope rules than the default Hermes-secret path.

reads.best: Combines local history, memory and explicit interests with explainable picks and actionable setup checks without installing or changing other plugins.
reads.worst: conflicts.check treats every memory-category plugin as an exclusive memory provider and recommends removing extras, which can misclassify compatible memory utilities.

reads.best: Payment path keeps approval outside the agent (digest match, loopback gateway, no signer, redacted results).
reads.worst: Needs separately run seller/directory/gateway servers; default public demo depends on one host.

reads.best: It directly improves agent trustworthiness by enforcing evidence checks at the final-output hook.
reads.worst: The checker covers only a few shallow claim families and has a small scenario suite, so its evidence matching can be over- or under-inclusive.

reads.best: Generative UI inside the chat with real round-trip interaction, a Python and browser validator kept in parity, and roughly 125 Python and 70 vitest tests.
reads.worst: The manifest says views load https images while the renderer also accepts http (including LAN hosts) and data: images, the README is short with no screenshots, the bundle is 2.1 MB, and no CI runs the tests.

reads.best: Bounded archive parsing, hidden-content canary tests and fingerprint-bound exports protect originals while keeping hidden values out of tool reports.
reads.worst: Protection covers only read_file in configured folders, and sharing snapshots discard formatting, images and other content rather than preserving a full document.

reads.best: Synchronizes real native input with character animations through a public computer-use provider while Hermes retains approval gating. [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AlleyBo55/hermes-chan/54041f8180c69f0d5100aee8bd87c623b89fb920/hermeschan/backend.py)
reads.worst: Requires a Rust/Tauri build and platform permissions, with native Wayland windows unsupported and Windows runtime behavior still unverified. [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AlleyBo55/hermes-chan/54041f8180c69f0d5100aee8bd87c623b89fb920/README.md)

reads.best: Deterministic detectors, checkpoint selection, intervention budgets and substantial process/recovery tests make the training supervisor much more than an occasional model-generated diagnosis.
reads.worst: The pinned ProcessHandle.launch passes the full Hermes environment to arbitrary trainers, exposing inherited secrets, and is_ours accepts a missing saved fingerprint when reattaching to a process ([nightshift/core/process.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Pavilion-devs/nightshift/8bbbd6e4163db347af5d4795134bfae22d036d4c/nightshift/core/process.py)).

reads.best: Code-enforced guardrails prevent the model from self-certifying a promise as done or exceeding user-set money/payee caps for consequences, backed by real unit tests.
reads.worst: A user can opt a promise into a 24-hour-cooloff 'locked' state that then fires a real consequence (payment or app block) without a fresh approval prompt on that specific miss.

reads.best: Local-first hybrid retrieval over many chat/mail archives and Korean HWP files, with setup/schedule/automate skills and a Desktop pane.
reads.worst: Launches an unpinned-transitive npx download of a large package and about 1.5 GB of models, with remote npm allowed; setup is heavy and the plugin itself contains little verifiable code.

reads.best: Three hooks put brand checks into the agent workflow, repairs are re-linted within a shared time budget, and tests include loading through Hermes PluginManager.
reads.worst: The guarantee exceeds enforcement: default reply checks require recognized fenced blocks, outbound checks depend on tool names and known text keys, and streaming is held only when explicitly enabled.

reads.best: Ships a complete interactive game, deterministic action validation, transactional saves and a council budget gate backed by broad simulation tests.

reads.best: Genuinely deep Desktop integration (composer middleware, steer/subagent RPCs, read-only state.db radar) with a large test suite and CI.

reads.best: A fresh, grounded take on keeping Hermes safe on its own hardware, with 36 tests on parsers, runway maths and policy and recorded live traces.
reads.worst: A single missed power reading moves PARKED to UNKNOWN and park state is never reloaded after restart, so paused cron jobs can stay paused despite the 'every park is undone' claim.

reads.best: A fresh idea: the agent gets measured feedback on the images, video and audio it just made, through one small, readable, fail-open hook with no network.
reads.worst: Only 5 tests (4 need ffmpeg), the README example relies on a probe.py that isn't included, and the path regex misses relative paths and paths with spaces.

reads.best: Turning an expensive vision-model desktop flow into a zero-token pixel-checked replay is a new and practical idea for agents.

reads.best: Four runtime hooks provide deterministic intervention, with redaction before audit previews and tested storage-failure fallbacks.

reads.best: Finished-product polish: demo video, screenshots, seven locales, clear no-network disclosure.

reads.best: Persistent typed records and tested, nonblocking context assembly make the agent’s everyday suggestions more personally informed.

reads.best: Fills a real gap in Hermes's rate-limited watch_patterns with its own wake budget and marks log text as untrusted.
reads.worst: No tests shipped in the plugin folder.
